thread:
maya: Bringing Eos-13B into the eval harness. Seeing a weird quality drop on q4f quant. Token splits look off and metrics are skewed.
samir: Can you paste a tiny example prompt + the tokenizer output? :eyes:
maya: Sure — minimal repro below. Running the tokenizer gives IDs but the runner collate seems to insert/shift a sentinel.
```
prompt = "Tell me a short poem about rivers"
# token ids (tokenizers): [50256, 123, 9876, 44, 11]
```
But runner logs show an extra sentinel inserted which shifts alignment for metrics.
jo: Is this happening for fp16 too or only q4f?
maya: FP16 looks fine. Only q4f shows the shift. Runner log snippet: `ERROR collate: padding sentinel mismatch - inserted <|sep|> at pos 3`
samir: That points at the eval-runner collate/chat-template path. We recently changed sentinel normalization in the tokenizer wrapper. @ci-bot did CI catch anything?
ci-bot: CI: test `eval_runner/tests/test_collate_chat.py::test_sentinel_normalization` failed on linux-py3.10 in PR #4821.
maya: PR #4821 was the tokenizer normalization refactor (cc @jo). Might be that `add_prefix_space` behavior changed and we now preserve leading spaces in some paths but strip them in others.
jo: Can you run a debug script and paste output? e.g. `python -m eval_runner.scripts.token_debug --model eos-13b --prompt "Tell me a short poem"`
maya: Ran it, trimmed output:
```
input_ids: [101, 345, 9999]
decoded: ' Tell me a short poem'
runner-collate: ['<BOS>', ' Tell', ' me', ' a', ' short', ' poem', '<EOS>']
```
Note the leading space on ' Tell' while other collate paths strip it.
samir: :thumbsup: tokenizer.decode preserves whitespace; our chat template wrapper sometimes normalizes with `strip()` but not everywhere. That inconsistency will shift token boundaries and break our quantized metric alignment since metrics assume same tokenization.
jo: Quick idea: change collate to rely on `tokenizer.tokenize(..., add_prefix_space=...)` and preserve the `add_prefix_space` flag per model. But need to be careful: some HF tokenizers require prefix.
maya: Also the quant CI uses kernel caching keyed on token sequences; any shift invalidates cached embeddings and skews metric logging. We should add a deterministic regression test: quantized path + chat template + short bench.
samir: I put together a checklist in the PR comments: 1) reproduce in a containerized env, 2) add unit test verifying token ids before/after collate are identical, 3) add a short integration job in CI that runs eos-13b q4f on a micro-benchmark, 4) add dashboard alert for sudden token-based metric deltas. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/4930
jo: Assigning to me for repro + unit test. @maya can you add a minimal failing example to the PR that asserts `pre_collate_ids == post_collate_ids`?
maya: Will add the example in 10m. FYI eval-bot already flagged a perf drop on staging: `perplexity +12%` after the last deploy.
eval-bot: eval-bot: Metric alert: `Eos-13B q4f - perplexity increased by 12.3% on small benchmark` — triggered 2026-03-19T14:08Z
samir: Timeline: jo will send a PR with the unit test and patch, maya will attach failing example, I'll add the CI job and a dashboard rule. If green, we can roll forward. :rocket:
jo: Found the root cause: `chat_template.apply()` was using `.strip()` in one codepath, which removed the add-prefix-space that some tokenizers expect. Fixing to preserve leading space when `add_prefix_space=True`. Patch incoming.
maya: Also ensuring `tokenizer.encode(..., add_special_tokens=False)` is used consistently to avoid double-special-token insertion.
samir: Thanks both. After merge I'll kick off distributed quant tests on Dedicated infra and re-run the small benchmark.
ci-bot: CI: new commit in PR #4930 triggered. Running `pytest eval_runner/tests/test_collate_chat.py::test_sentinel_normalization -q`.
